QUIC interop test and benchmark commands for Firedancer and Agave.

# Purpose
This file is a command-line test and benchmark driver for QUIC traffic between Firedancer and Agave components. It sets up local UDP sockets, Firedancer workspace and `fd_quic_t` objects, and Solana `ConnectionCache` or `spawn_server` endpoints, then runs one of several modes from `main`: `blast`, `ping-server`, `ping-client`, or `spam-server`. The code uses unsafe FFI bindings from `bindings` to connect Firedancer UDP and QUIC layers, start and service the network stack, and check connection state and metrics.

The helper functions `agave_to_fdquic`, `agave_to_fdquic_bench`, and `fdquic_to_agave` each build one side of the link and drive traffic in a loop. `agave_to_fdquic` sends a small payload from Agave to a Firedancer QUIC server and checks packet and connection counters. `agave_to_fdquic_bench` sends repeated batches of random MTU-sized payloads and can write PCAP output when `PCAP` is set. `fdquic_to_agave` starts an Agave QUIC server, creates a Firedancer QUIC client, and waits for the connection to reach `ACTIVE` or `DEAD`. The file also defines `new_udp_socket` and a small wrapper for `fd_wksp_new_anon` to simplify setup of the FFI objects used by the test modes.
